evidence.ref: The non-LLM mirror RUNNER (.warp/tracker_mirror_runner.py) DRIVES the shipped one-way mirror onto a tracker and adds NO mirror logic of its own. reconcile(events, config, spec_index, plan_index, adapter) is the pure core: it materializes the stream once (a generator is single-pass) and feeds BOTH mirror_events (the spec lifecycle: status, comments, artifact links, and the ready-to-test reassignment) and mirror_plan_events (the plan structure: epic + children) from tracker_mirror.py (WARP-0605/0606 + the WARP-1004 reassign/links). run_from_repo(adapter, read_events=..., config=..., spec_index=..., plan_index=...) is the thin production wrapper that reads the stream through an INJECTED event-stream reader (the durable .warp/events.jsonl via _default_event_reader in production, a fixture list in the gate) and loads the tracker config and the spec/plan indices from the REPOSITORY (load_tracker_config, build_spec_index, build_plan_index, the source of truth). It is a RECONCILER (recompute the desired tracker state each pass and apply it), idempotent under replay with NO processed-offset ledger and NO second store, and it writes ONLY through the injected adapter (the tracker); no path mutates a spec or plan definition.

selftest (scripts/selftest.py, the WARP-1005 block) drives the runner over the FakeTracker with a fixture stream: reconcile over a growing stream walks child:PLAN-0010:W5 through the mapped statuses (To Do, In Review, Done) and reassigns at ready-to-test; and run_from_repo, given an INJECTED reader (asserted called exactly once with the fixture path, so the stream is parsed exactly one way) and injected spec/plan indices, drives BOTH mirrors from ONE stream (the spec's child reaches Done AND the plan's epic:PLAN-0010 is created with warp_repo repo-a), proving the wrapper feeds both and adds no logic.

The runner is OPT-IN and OFF BY DEFAULT. It is invoked explicitly as a warp CLI subcommand over the runner: bin/warp gains `mirror` in KNOWN_SUBCOMMANDS and a route that calls tracker_mirror_runner._cli (byte-identical across plugin/templates and all six packs). Installing WARP creates NO timer, daemon, or auto-start, and nothing runs the runner on its own; each invocation is ONE reconcile pass (poll-when-run) and a cadence, if wanted, is the operator's own poll interval when they run it again, never a hidden background mechanism. It spawns NO detached or headless process (feedback_no_rogue_processes / PLAN-0007 NG1): the module imports no process-spawning module and has no scheduler, the same structural posture as the fleet supervisor (WARP-0907). The boundary is documented in the module docstring, the CLI help, and the capability note. Because the runner is repo-only build machinery (like the other tracker_*.py modules), bin/warp checks for its presence and fails loud and honestly in a pack that did not lay it rather than import a missing module.

Idempotency is proven offline over the FakeTracker with TEETH (scripts/selftest.py, WARP-1005 block, no network): a GROWING event stream advances the ticket (pass 1 ready-only -> mapped ready with no reassign; pass 2 ready+verdict -> in_review, reassigned to the reviewer once, artifact links posted once; pass 3 ready+verdict+shipped -> mapped shipped); and a full REPLAY plus a DOUBLED event records NO new transition, comment, or reassignment (transitions == 0, comments == 0, reassignments == 0) and leaves the tracker state byte-identical (state_digest unchanged). NON-TAUTOLOGY: on a fresh tracker the ready-only stream stays at the mapped ready status with NO assignee, and only the grown stream (with the verdict) advances and reassigns, so the advance is caused by the growing stream, not by the runner always writing. There is no processed-offset ledger and no second store; the events are the truth and the tracker converges to them.

The runner drives only the FakeTracker in the gate (an in-memory tracker with no network and no credentials); the assertions above compute the desired projection from the stream each pass and apply it, exactly matching the reconciler contract the runner inherits from mirror_events / mirror_plan_events. The live JiraCloud path is reference-only and never runs here.
